## TL;DR

Addressed the remaining review finding in task #1070. During the shell cross-fade, Vue temporarily keeps the outgoing loading shell and the incoming routed page mounted together. Because both were ordinary flex children of `.main`, they divided its available height until the fade ended; the incoming page then expanded, creating a visible layout jump. The leaving shell now overlays the pane absolutely and no longer participates in flex sizing. `.main` is its positioning context. A regression assertion in `app-loading-skeleton.test.ts` checks both CSS conditions while the transition harness confirms the outgoing shell remains mounted until leave completes.

The changed-path RepoOS check passed after formatting the test. Remote validation rebuilt the application, ran the changed-path suite, completed the rendered contrast audit, and passed UI smoke. The subsequent local guard run also passed formatting, lint, build freshness, CSS/theme/color checks, contrast, bare-require, task-asset, and UI smoke checks.

## Work and rationale

The review finding was about geometry, not whether both transition elements coexist. The incoming route must continue to occupy the pane's full flex height while the shell fades out above it. I therefore kept the existing Vue transition behavior and changed only the outgoing transition layer: `position: absolute`, `inset: 0`, `width: 100%`, `flex: none`, and `pointer-events: none`. Making `.main` `position: relative` anchors that overlay to the routed pane. The pointer rule lets interaction reach the incoming page during the short fade. Reduced-motion behavior continues to disable the opacity transition as before.

The test now reads the shared stylesheet and asserts that the leaving class is absolute, covers the pane, and cannot flex-shrink or grow; it also asserts `.main` establishes the containing block. The transition harness still verifies that both incoming content and the outgoing shell coexist until the leave callback completes. These checks cover the transition's intended lifecycle and its layout contract. The visual smoke check passed against the built UI.

The task’s broader layout audit was already implemented in the preceding work on this branch. The audit below records the real content pattern against the selected first-load placeholder shape; data placeholders appear beneath the live page chrome. `PageSkeleton` keeps counts tied to shared layout constants and uses minimal row placeholders where a more detailed data layout would be misleading.

| Route/page group | Real content layout | Skeleton shape and audit outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Control (`/`) | Dashboard sections and summary blocks, not a task board | One dashboard-shaped block; avoids the old auto-fit set of tall cards and stray wrapped card. |
| Stories | A single list of story rows with toolbar/header chrome | Rows; one row/list region, no unrelated card grid. |
| Work | Multi-column task board, responsive columns | Board placeholders use the shared work-column count and breakpoint. |
| Inputs and Client Board | Input cards arranged in the input-board columns | Input-board placeholders use the shared input-column count. |
| Checks | Tabular run/check data | Table skeleton, matching the data region rather than generic cards. |
| Agents | Agent cards | Cards, matching the card collection. |
| Releases | Release/distribution data with tabular/list regions | Table/row placeholders aligned to the relevant view content. |
| Deployments | Deployment environment and binding panels | Deployment-shaped placeholders. |
| Dev | Configured targets | Target rows/cards matching the target list. |
| Secrets | Secret metadata list | Rows; values remain undisclosed and chrome stays live. |
| Settings | Sections and forms | Minimal rows for loading data; static settings navigation and controls are not skeletonized. |
| Other registered routes | Route-specific content varies; simple detail and utility screens do not benefit from fabricated grids | Explicit route mapping uses rows or the smallest suitable shape, avoiding excess placeholder items. |

The route mapping is exercised against the router's registered paths, and skeleton-kind tests assert counts against shared constants. The timing, cache, and reduced-motion behavior is covered by the existing `PageSkeleton`/shell tests in this branch; this review fix did not change those behaviors.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the reviewed transition through `App.vue`, the `.main` flex rules, and the shell transition CSS. The existing test only proved that Vue retained both elements during leave, which explains why it missed the height change. I considered changing the transition to remove the outgoing element immediately, but that would discard the cross-fade already required by the UX. Keeping both elements with the outgoing one absolutely positioned preserves the fade while leaving the incoming route as the sole flex-sized child. I added CSS-contract assertions alongside the lifecycle assertion so a future CSS edit cannot silently restore the in-flow overlap.

## Challenges and blockers

The first required check completed remote validation successfully but failed the local formatting guard because the new assertion needed the repository formatter's line wrapping. I ran `bun run fmt` and repeated the required check. The second remote run encountered a hung ThinkPad validation container and RepoOS retried on the Bee runner; that retry completed successfully. No source or check failures remain. The worktree stays on the task branch for RepoOS handoff processing.

## Key learnings

A transition lifecycle test can pass while the user-visible geometry is wrong. For routed content inside flex layouts, keeping an outgoing layer mounted requires explicitly removing it from flow and anchoring it to the pane; otherwise both children share the same constrained height. The regression test now records both facts. The check's remote test phase and local guard phase are distinct: the former ran the broad changed-path suite and UI checks, while the latter confirmed formatting and source guards on the current worktree tree.
